w: The Retezat Mountains are among the highest massifs in Romania, part of the Southern Carpathians in Hunedoara County. Their highest peak, Peleaga, reaches 2,509m; Papusa and Retezat Peak follow close behind. The range's name means 'cut off' in Romanian, a nod to the abrupt, glacially sheared profile of its ridgelines.
s: Romania's high Carpathians, cut off by name and by cliffs
_facts: Highest peak Peleaga, 2,509m; also Papusa and Retezat Peak

w: Lake Bucura is a glacier cirque lake at the base of Peleaga Peak in the Retezat Mountains, sitting at about 2,040m. It is Romania's largest glacial lake, covering over 105,000 square metres, 550m long with an average width of 160m and a maximum width of 225m. Its deepest point reaches 15.5m, holding a total volume of around 625,000 cubic metres.
_facts: Romania's largest glacial lake, ~105,000 sq m, at ~2,040m altitude
550m long, up to 15.5m deep, volume ~625,000 cubic metres

w: Peleaga is the highest point in the Retezat Mountains at 2,509m, in Hunedoara County within historic Transylvania. It rises above Lake Bucura, Romania's largest glacial lake at 2,030m and 8.9 hectares, and stands alongside the range's other named summits, Papusa and Retezat Peak, within the Retezat National Park - Romania's first.
s: The Retezat's roof, 2,509m above Bucura Lake
_facts: 2,509m, highest point in the Retezat Mountains
Overlooks Lake Bucura, Romania's largest glacial lake

w: Papusa stands 2,508m in the Retezat Mountains of the Southern Carpathians, Romania - the range's second-highest peak, just a single metre short of Peleaga. It overlooks Lake Bucura, the country's largest glacial lake at 2,030m, within Retezat National Park, Romania's first protected national park.
s: Second-highest Retezat summit, a metre below Peleaga
_facts: 2,508m, second-highest peak in the Retezat range, 1m below Peleaga
Within Retezat National Park, Romania's first national park

a: Raul Mare valley, southwest of Hateg
w: Gura Apelor Dam, a rock-fill structure on the Raul Mare river about 35km southwest of Hateg, is Romania's tallest dam. Built between 1975 and 1986, it feeds the underground Raul Mare hydroelectric plant 18km away through a 582.5m hydraulic head, generating 335 megawatts. In 2012 its reservoir was drained for repairs, expected to refill in 2014.
s: Romania's tallest dam, its reservoir drained in 2012
_facts: Feeds a 335 MW underground hydro plant via a 582.5m head

w: The Valcan Mountains run about 54 kilometres through Gorj County, part of the Retezat-Godeanu group in the Southern Carpathians. Their highest point, Oslea Peak, reaches 1,946m, with Straja close behind at 1,848m. The range runs the length of the Jiu Valley, forming a natural barrier along its southern side.
s: A 54km ridge walling off the Jiu Valley's south side
_facts: 54km range, part of the Retezat-Godeanu group
Highest points Oslea Peak (1,946m) and Straja (1,848m)
Forms the southern wall of the Jiu Valley

w: Founded in 1935, Retezat National Park was Romania's first national park and remains a category II IUCN protected area in the Retezat Mountains. It holds over 1,000 plant species and some of Europe's last pristine old-growth forest. Decades of protection have not stopped rising pressure from logging and sheep-grazing, which now threaten its status as public land.
_facts: Over 1,000 plant species; pristine old-growth forest
Facing pressure from logging and grazing encroachment
